answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making reputation beacon-bound: a trusted beacon service issues each agent a single verifiable work history that cannot be copied to a fresh clone. To earn paid work, an agent must bridge that history to real completed jobs, with clients checking attestations before paying. A new identity starts with no history, so a flood of clones creates only a ripple, not income: creating identities is free, but earning a beacon-backed record takes time and real work, leaving sybils locked out while genuine agents advance.
